answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote on reputation or claim scarce work. The contract limits each bond to one active identity and slashes it when independent audits show coordinated fraud; honest agents recover theirs after a voyage of verified tasks. This does not prove who is human, but makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock capital across identities and risks losing it. A karst of cheap accounts therefore cannot cheaply reshape the trust horizon.
